reason: Section 94 is a focused effect rule for registered development charge agreements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Binding effect and filing of development charge agreements

evidenceText: is binding

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that a development charge agreement binds land and lots as specified, becomes effective only when certified copies are filed, and binds subsequent owners until discharge.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how development charge agreements bind land and later owners and when they become effective.

reason: Section 95 defines the key term used in the incentive or bonus zoning agreement Division.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Meaning of incentive or bonus zoning agreement

evidenceText: means an agreement that permits the relaxation

proposedGroups.reason: The section defines an incentive or bonus zoning agreement as an agreement relaxing zoning requirements when the applicant exceeds other requirements or undertakes public-interest action.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what an incentive or bonus zoning agreement permits and what the applicant must exceed or undertake.

reason: Section 96 covers several distinct incentive or bonus zoning topics: by-law authority and certification, by-law contents, agreement terms and binding effect, and money in lieu.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incentive or bonus zoning by-law authority, preparation, and certification

evidenceText: may by by-law provide for an incentive or bonus zoning agreement

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-laws where a municipal or rural plan is in effect and set preparation and certification requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council may make an incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-law and how it must be prepared and certified.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required contents of incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-laws

evidenceText: An incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-law shall

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 96(2) requires the by-law to identify eligible developments and areas, matters council may consider, and the method for determining the contribution.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what an incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-law must identify or set out.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incentive or bonus zoning agreement contents, discharge, filing, and binding effect

evidenceText: shall not become effective until certified copies

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections describe what an agreement may include, discharge options, filing before effectiveness, binding effect on later owners, and that the by-law does not require council to enter an agreement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what incentive or bonus zoning agreements may include, when they bind later owners, and why council is not required to enter one.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Money in lieu of incentive or bonus zoning contributions

evidenceText: paid into a special account

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow money in lieu of a contribution and require it to be held in a special account and spent only for the accepted purpose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how money accepted in lieu of an incentive or bonus zoning contribution must be handled.

reason: Section 97 provides substantive validity and commencement conditions for an incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incentive or bonus zoning by-law validity and filing commencement

evidenceText: No incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-law is valid unless

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify certification, section 111 compliance, paragraph 112(1)(b) compliance, and commencement on filing or a later by-law date.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the validity requirements for an incentive or bonus zoning agreement by-law and when it comes into force.

reason: Section 98 is a direct prohibition against breaching incentive or bonus zoning agreements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibition on breaching incentive or bonus zoning agreements

evidenceText: No person shall breach

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that no person shall breach the terms of an incentive or bonus zoning agreement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prohibition against breaching incentive or bonus zoning agreement terms.

reason: Section 99 separates the permitted contents of local government agreements from plan-amendment and filing duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local government agreement subjects for joint planning, services, contributions, and disputes

evidenceText: joint land use planning and development matters

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 99(1) lists what a local government agreement by-law may adopt, including joint planning matters, dispute mechanisms, covered services or infrastructure, expense contributions, amendment or termination processes, and development matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the subjects that may be included in a local government agreement adopted by by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Plan amendments and Minister filings for local government agreements

evidenceText: Within 30 days

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require plans or zoning by-laws to reflect land development controls and require certified copies to be filed with the Minister within 30 days after entry, amendment, or termination.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when local government agreements require planning document amendments and what certified copies must be filed with the Minister.

reason: Section 100 provides substantive validity and commencement conditions for a local government agreement by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local government agreement by-law validity and filing commencement

evidenceText: No local government agreement by-law is valid unless

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify section 111 compliance, paragraph 112(1)(b) compliance, and commencement on filing or a later by-law date.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the validity requirements for a local government agreement by-law and when it comes into force.

reason: Section 101 is a focused authority for development scheme by-laws tied to an existing municipal or rural plan.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development scheme by-law to carry out or amplify plan proposals

evidenceText: may make a by-law adopting a development scheme

proposedGroups.reason: The section allows council to adopt a development scheme to carry out or amplify a proposal in a plan or a project not inconsistent with the plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council may adopt a development scheme and what plan-related proposals or projects it may carry out or amplify.

reason: Section 102 is a large development scheme source with distinct required contents, optional powers, authorizations, agreements, and cost rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required written material, affected land, development details, implementation, reserved land, and subdivision manner

evidenceText: shall

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 102(1)(a) requires written statements, maps, drawings, affected land, development details, implementation method, reserved land, and subdivision manner.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the required contents a development scheme must include.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development scheme alteration, acquisition, public sites, land allocation, timing, Minister matters, and plan effects

evidenceText: may, in relation to the scheme area

proposedGroups.reason: These provisions authorize optional controls over alterations, permits, land acquisition or agreements, public service sites, allocation and timing, require Minister-requested general matters, and apply municipal plan notice and effect rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the optional land, building, acquisition, public-site, allocation, timing, Minister-matter, and plan-effect rules for development schemes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development scheme authorizations, owner agreements, filing, binding effect, and costs

evidenceText: shall not become effective until certified copies

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow council to authorize construction or repairs despite the scheme, enter and file binding agreements, and treat acquisition or other expenses and sale proceeds as part of the scheme cost.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council may authorize work or agreements under a development scheme and how scheme costs and proceeds are treated.

reason: Section 103 provides substantive validity and commencement conditions for a development scheme by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development scheme by-law validity and filing commencement

evidenceText: No development scheme by-law is valid unless

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify section 111 compliance, paragraph 112(1)(b) compliance, and commencement on filing or a later by-law date.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the validity requirements for a development scheme by-law and when it comes into force.

reason: Section 104 is a direct priority rule for conflicts between a development scheme and listed land-use controls.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development scheme priority over zoning, subdivision, or rural plan zoning provisions

evidenceText: the development scheme shall prevail

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that a development scheme prevails over a conflicting zoning by-law, subdivision by-law, or zoning provisions in a rural plan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which instrument prevails when a development scheme conflicts with zoning, subdivision, or rural-plan zoning provisions.

reason: Section 105 is a coherent local-government land acquisition rule for carrying out plan or scheme proposals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local government acquisition of land for plan or scheme proposals

evidenceText: may acquire by gift, purchase, expropriation or otherwise

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections authorize acquisition by gift, purchase, expropriation or otherwise, list included land types, and require expropriation under the Local Governance Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what land or interests a local government may acquire for planning proposals and how expropriation is undertaken.

reason: Section 106 is a coherent Ministerial land acquisition rule for regional or rural plan and regulation proposals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister acquisition of land for regional, rural, or regulation proposals

evidenceText: the Minister may acquire by gift, purchase, expropriation or otherwise

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections authorize the Minister to acquire land or interests for listed plans and regulations, apply local-government land categories with modifications, and require Expropriation Act process.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what land or interests the Minister may acquire for planning proposals and how expropriation is undertaken.

reason: Section 107 is a focused compensation rule for unauthorized development after notice of a plan or scheme.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compensation exclusion for unauthorized development after plan or scheme notice

evidenceText: compensation for the land on expropriation shall not include

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections exclude compensation for unauthorized development after notice of intention and allow a court order for compensation where development was undertaken in good faith without knowledge of the restriction.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when compensation excludes unauthorized post-notice development and when a judge may order compensation anyway.

reason: Section 108 is a large development-approval source with distinct topics for approval requirement, conformity checks, temporary controls, posting/exemptions, unlawful subdivision, and delegation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development approval required before development or building permit

evidenceText: no person shall undertake a development

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 108(0.1) prohibits undertaking development or issuing a building permit unless the development officer grants approval.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the general rule requiring development officer approval before development or a building permit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development officer conformity checks before granting approval

evidenceText: Before granting an approval for a development

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 108(1) requires the development officer to ensure conformity or compliance with regional plans, municipal or rural plans, development schemes, by-laws, agreements, land-use policy regulations, and prescribed requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the plans, by-laws, agreements, regulations, and other requirements checked before development approval.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: End of pending controls, permit posting, and exempt development types

evidenceText: shall be posted in a prominent place

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state when pending-plan or by-law controls cease, require permits or approvals to be posted, and exclude exempted development types.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when pending controls stop applying, what must be posted on the property, and which development types are exempt from section 108.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Unlawful subdivision ownership check and development officer delegation

evidenceText: has reason to believe that land has been subdivided

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections bar approval where there is reason to believe land was unlawfully subdivided unless ownership or agency is established, and allow certain planning directors to delegate section 108 powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the ownership check for land suspected of unlawful subdivision and who may delegate development approval powers.

reason: Section 109 is a coherent by-law-making procedure and voting rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: By-law readings, majority votes, and mayor or presiding officer vote

evidenceText: the provisions of section 15 of the Local Governance Act apply

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections apply Local Governance Act by-law procedure, allow plan or scheme document readings instead of full by-law readings, state when third reading by title satisfies majority vote requirements, and allow one vote by the mayor or presiding officer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special reading and voting rules for making by-laws under the Act.
